card.name: Syrtos
card.tagline: One of the oldest, most widespread Greek chain dances.
card.profile: A collective name for a family of Greek folk dances; open circle/curving line, dancers link hands facing right, led by a leader who improvises and may break away. Among the most ancient Greek dances, described by Lucian (c. AD 125-190). Mainland versions (Peloponnese, Thessaly, Macedonia, Thrace) use 7/8; Crete, the Aegean, Asia Minor and Constantinople use 4/4 (slow-quick-quick). Traditionally segregated lines of men and women, the leader holding the second dancer by a handkerchief; played on regional instruments (Cretan lyra/violin, laouto, clarinet). Central to weddings and religious festivals (English Wikipedia; Britannica).
card.insight: Syrtos and kalamatianos share identical steps but differ in meter (4/4 vs 7/8); the name derives from syro, 'to drag/lead' (English Wikipedia; Britannica).
